title: Maryland's 1st Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Maryland's 1st Congressional District will be decided in a general election on November 3, 2026, following a primary on June 23, 2026. The district covers the entire Eastern Shore of Maryland, including Salisbury, Harford County, and parts of northern Baltimore County. Incumbent Republican Andy Harris, the chair of the House Freedom Caucus who has held the seat since 2011, faces a Republican primary challenge from Chris Bruneau, while four Democrats—Victor Guidice, Dan Schwartz, George Walish, and Randi White—are competing in the Democratic primary. The race is rated 'Solid R' by Cook Political Report due to the district's Republican lean, though Democrats are energized by Harris's role in efforts to overturn the 2020 election results.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Andy Harris
candidates.summary: Andy Harris is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Maryland's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2010 and currently serving his eighth term. He serves as chair of the House Freedom Caucus and is the only Republican in Maryland's congressional delegation. Before Congress, he was an anesthesiologist at Johns Hopkins Hospital and served in the Maryland Senate from 1999 to 2011.

candidates.name: Chris Bruneau
candidates.summary: Chris Bruneau is a building contractor and Republican candidate challenging incumbent Andy Harris in the primary. A former U.S. Army deep-sea diver who served in Panama and Germany, he owns a Paul Davis Restoration franchise in Bel Air, Maryland. He previously ran for this seat in 2024 and has pledged to support term limits on Congress.

candidates.name: Dan Schwartz
candidates.summary: Dan Schwartz is a consumer advocate and Democratic candidate for Maryland's 1st Congressional District. With over 14 years of experience working in financial regulation to protect consumers from financial abuse and corruption, he is running on a platform of affordability, restoring consumer protections, and prioritizing the health and safety of Eastern Shore residents. He studied political science at George Washington University.

candidates.name: Randi White
candidates.summary: Randi White is a Democratic candidate for Maryland's 1st Congressional District who was born and raised in Salisbury. With over 20 years of experience in media and communications, she is running on a detailed 181-page policy platform covering healthcare, environmental justice, and economic opportunity. White is the only candidate in the Democratic primary who was born and raised in the district.

candidates.name: Victor Guidice
candidates.summary: Victor Guidice is a Democratic candidate for Maryland's 1st Congressional District who describes himself as a husband, father, minister, and fourth-generation resident of Harford County. He has worked as a commercial truck driver and emphasizes his experience overcoming job insecurity, homelessness, and food insecurity. His platform focuses on lowering the cost of living, universal childcare, universal healthcare, and restoring constitutional rights.

summary_sources.title: Victor A Guidice candidate profile - WBOC

candidates.name: George Walish
candidates.summary: George Walish is a Democratic candidate for Maryland's 1st Congressional District who has lived on the Eastern Shore for nearly 30 years. His career includes work as a construction worker in various building trades, a junior high school social studies teacher and coach, and 30 years as a senior executive in the automobile industry. He is a former Saint Michaels town commissioner and founded the St. Michaels Concours d'Elegance.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race as of June 2026, which limits confidence. However, the structural indicators strongly favor the Republican incumbent: Andy Harris has held the seat since 2011 (eight terms), the district is rated 'Solid R' by Cook Political Report, and Harris chairs the House Freedom Caucus. The Democratic field is fragmented among four candidates (Schwartz, White, Guidice, Walish) with no clear consensus leader, and the Republican primary challenger (Bruneau) previously ran and lost in 2024. The district's Eastern Shore geography has a strong Republican baseline. Given incumbency, district partisanship, and a divided Democratic field, Republicans hold an overwhelming advantage—but the complete absence of polling data prevents a high-confidence rating.
